title: Clinical outcome and implant survival after alternate surgery knee sled prosthesis on total knee endoprosthesis
summary:
The implantation of a sled prosthesis (unicondylar knee arthroplasty, UKA) is an established and successful procedure in today's orthopaedics. The operation can be performed minimally invasive, has a relatively low rate of complications and shows 10-year survival rates of over 90% in many studies. 
However, the different endoprosthesis registers still show higher revision and failure rates for UKA in direct comparison to the bicondylar total knee arthroplasty (TKA or KTEP). The implantation of a sled prosthesis is still very complex from an operational point of view and still clearly dependent on the experience of the surgeon. The failure of a sled prosthesis is usually followed by the surgical change to a total endoprosthesis. In this study, patients who had a change from a sled prosthesis to a total knee endoprosthesis will be interviewed to investigate the so-called implant survival and the revision rate. Furthermore, patient satisfaction and the subjective function of the joint will be investigated by means of questionnaires. In addition, the radiological images already taken will be analysed with regard to common radiological criteria of knee endoprosthetics (loosening, joint and implant position).
conditions: Presence of a knee joint prosthesis

interventions.name:
Patients who have undergone an alternating operation from UKA (unicondylar knee arthroplasty) to TKA (total knee arthroplasty).
Initially, the physicians will contact the patients by phone in order to be informed about the non-invasive study and to be able to answer questions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Male or female patients in the age group ≥ 18 years 
- Changeover operation "UKA to TKA" carried out
Exclusion criteria:
- Renewed revision of the knee TEP with replacement of individual or all components
